clauses.normalized_text: To aid debugging, HTTP caches often append header fields to a response, explaining how they handled the request in an ad hoc manner.
clauses.raw_text: To aid debugging, HTTP caches often append header fields to a response, explaining how they handled the request in an ad hoc manner.

clauses.normalized_text: This specification defines a standard mechanism to do so that is aligned with HTTP's caching model.
clauses.raw_text: This specification defines a standard mechanism to do so that is aligned with HTTP's caching model.

clauses.normalized_text: To aid debugging (both by humans and automated tools), HTTP caches often append header fields to a response explaining how they handled the request.
clauses.raw_text: To aid debugging (both by humans and automated tools), HTTP caches often append header fields to a response explaining how they handled the request.

clauses.normalized_text: Unfortunately, the semantics of these header fields are often unclear, and both the semantics and syntax used vary between implementations.
clauses.raw_text: Unfortunately, the semantics of these header fields are often unclear, and both the semantics and syntax used vary between implementations.

clauses.normalized_text: This specification defines a new HTTP response header field, "Cache-Status", for this purpose with standardized syntax and semantics.
clauses.raw_text: This specification defines a new HTTP response header field, "Cache-Status", for this purpose with standardized syntax and semantics.

clauses.normalized_text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
clauses.raw_text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

clauses.normalized_text: This document uses the following terminology from Section 3 of [STRUCTURED-FIELDS] to specify syntax and parsing: List, String, Token, Integer, and Boolean.
clauses.raw_text: This document uses the following terminology from Section 3 of [STRUCTURED-FIELDS] to specify syntax and parsing: List, String, Token, Integer, and Boolean.

clauses.normalized_text: This document also uses terminology from [HTTP] and [HTTP-CACHING].
clauses.raw_text: This document also uses terminology from [HTTP] and [HTTP-CACHING].

clauses.normalized_text: The Cache-Status HTTP response header field indicates how caches have handled that response and its corresponding request.
clauses.raw_text: The Cache-Status HTTP response header field indicates how caches have handled that response and its corresponding request.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: The syntax of this header field conforms to [STRUCTURED-FIELDS].
clauses.raw_text: The syntax of this header field conforms to [STRUCTURED-FIELDS].
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: Its value is a List.
clauses.raw_text: Its value is a List.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: Each member of the List represents a cache that has handled the request.
clauses.raw_text: Each member of the List represents a cache that has handled the request.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: The first member represents the cache closest to the origin server, and the last member represents the cache closest to the user (possibly including the user agent's cache itself if it appends a value).
clauses.raw_text: The first member represents the cache closest to the origin server, and the last member represents the cache closest to the user (possibly including the user agent's cache itself if it appends a value).
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: Caches determine when it is appropriate to add the Cache-Status header field to a response.
clauses.raw_text: Caches determine when it is appropriate to add the Cache-Status header field to a response.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: Some might add it to all responses, whereas others might only do so when specifically configured to, or when the request contains a header field that activates a debugging mode.
clauses.raw_text: Some might add it to all responses, whereas others might only do so when specifically configured to, or when the request contains a header field that activates a debugging mode.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: See Section 6 for related security considerations.
clauses.raw_text: See Section 6 for related security considerations.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: An intermediary SHOULD NOT append a Cache-Status member to responses that it generates locally, even if that intermediary contains a cache, unless the generated response is based upon a stored response (e.g., 304 (Not Modified) and 206 (Partial Content) are both based upon a stored response).
clauses.raw_text: An intermediary SHOULD NOT append a Cache-Status member to responses that it generates locally, even if that intermediary contains a cache, unless the generated response is based upon a stored response (e.g., 304 (Not Modified) and 206 (Partial Content) are both based upon a stored response).
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: For example, a proxy generating a 400 response due to a malformed request will not add a Cache-Status value, because that response was generated by the proxy, not the origin server.
clauses.raw_text: For example, a proxy generating a 400 response due to a malformed request will not add a Cache-Status value, because that response was generated by the proxy, not the origin server.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: When adding a value to the Cache-Status header field, caches SHOULD preserve the existing field value, to allow debugging of the entire chain of caches handling the request.
clauses.raw_text: When adding a value to the Cache-Status header field, caches SHOULD preserve the existing field value, to allow debugging of the entire chain of caches handling the request.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: Each List member identifies the cache that inserted it, and this identifier MUST be a String or Token.
clauses.raw_text: Each List member identifies the cache that inserted it, and this identifier MUST be a String or Token.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: Depending on the deployment, this might be a product or service name (e.g., "ExampleCache" or "Example CDN"), a hostname ("cache-3.example.com"), an IP address, or a generated string.
clauses.raw_text: Depending on the deployment, this might be a product or service name (e.g., "ExampleCache" or "Example CDN"), a hostname ("cache-3.example.com"), an IP address, or a generated string.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: Each member of the list can have parameters that describe that cache's handling of the request.
clauses.raw_text: Each member of the list can have parameters that describe that cache's handling of the request.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: While these parameters are OPTIONAL, caches are encouraged to provide as much information as possible.
clauses.raw_text: While these parameters are OPTIONAL, caches are encouraged to provide as much information as possible.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: This specification defines the following parameters.
clauses.raw_text: This specification defines the following parameters.
clauses.section_heading: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field

clauses.normalized_text: The value of "hit" is a Boolean that, when true, indicates that the request was satisfied by the cache; that is, it was not forwarded, and the response was obtained from the cache.
clauses.raw_text: The value of "hit" is a Boolean that, when true, indicates that the request was satisfied by the cache; that is, it was not forwarded, and the response was obtained from the cache.

clauses.normalized_text: A response that was originally produced by the origin but was modified by the cache (for example, a 304 or 206 status code) is still considered a hit, as long as it did not go forward (e.g., for validation).
clauses.raw_text: A response that was originally produced by the origin but was modified by the cache (for example, a 304 or 206 status code) is still considered a hit, as long as it did not go forward (e.g., for validation).

clauses.normalized_text: A response that was in cache but not able to be used without going forward (e.g., because it was stale or partial) is not considered a hit.
clauses.raw_text: A response that was in cache but not able to be used without going forward (e.g., because it was stale or partial) is not considered a hit.

clauses.normalized_text: Note that a stale response that is used without going forward (e.g., because the origin server is not available) can be considered a hit.
clauses.raw_text: Note that a stale response that is used without going forward (e.g., because the origin server is not available) can be considered a hit.

clauses.normalized_text: "hit" and "fwd" are exclusive; only one of them should appear on each list member.
clauses.raw_text: "hit" and "fwd" are exclusive; only one of them should appear on each list member.

clauses.normalized_text: "fwd", when present, indicates that the request went forward towards the origin; its value is a Token that indicates why.
clauses.raw_text: "fwd", when present, indicates that the request went forward towards the origin; its value is a Token that indicates why.

clauses.normalized_text: The following parameter values are defined to explain why the request went forward, from most specific to least:
clauses.raw_text: The following parameter values are defined to explain why the request went forward, from most specific to least:

clauses.normalized_text: bypass: The cache was configured to not handle this request.
clauses.raw_text: bypass: The cache was configured to not handle this request.

clauses.normalized_text: method: The request method's semantics require the request to be forwarded.
clauses.raw_text: method: The request method's semantics require the request to be forwarded.

clauses.normalized_text: uri-miss: The cache did not contain any responses that matched the request URI.
clauses.raw_text: uri-miss: The cache did not contain any responses that matched the request URI.

clauses.normalized_text: vary-miss: The cache contained a response that matched the request URI, but it could not select a response based upon this request's header fields and stored Vary header fields.
clauses.raw_text: vary-miss: The cache contained a response that matched the request URI, but it could not select a response based upon this request's header fields and stored Vary header fields.

clauses.normalized_text: miss: The cache did not contain any responses that could be used to satisfy this request (to be used when an implementation cannot distinguish between uri-miss and vary-miss).
clauses.raw_text: miss: The cache did not contain any responses that could be used to satisfy this request (to be used when an implementation cannot distinguish between uri-miss and vary-miss).

clauses.normalized_text: request: The cache was able to select a fresh response for the request, but the request's semantics (e.g., Cache-Control request directives) did not allow its use.
clauses.raw_text: request: The cache was able to select a fresh response for the request, but the request's semantics (e.g., Cache-Control request directives) did not allow its use.

clauses.normalized_text: stale: The cache was able to select a response for the request, but it was stale.
clauses.raw_text: stale: The cache was able to select a response for the request, but it was stale.

clauses.normalized_text: partial: The cache was able to select a partial response for the request, but it did not contain all of the requested ranges (or the request was for the complete response).
clauses.raw_text: partial: The cache was able to select a partial response for the request, but it did not contain all of the requested ranges (or the request was for the complete response).

clauses.normalized_text: The most specific reason known to the cache SHOULD be used, to the extent that it is possible to implement.
clauses.raw_text: The most specific reason known to the cache SHOULD be used, to the extent that it is possible to implement.

clauses.normalized_text: See also [HTTP-CACHING], Section 4.
clauses.raw_text: See also [HTTP-CACHING], Section 4.

clauses.normalized_text: The value of "fwd-status" is an Integer that indicates which status code (see [HTTP], Section 15) the next-hop server returned in response to the forwarded request.
clauses.raw_text: The value of "fwd-status" is an Integer that indicates which status code (see [HTTP], Section 15) the next-hop server returned in response to the forwarded request.

clauses.normalized_text: The fwd-status parameter is only meaningful when fwd is present.
clauses.raw_text: The fwd-status parameter is only meaningful when fwd is present.

clauses.normalized_text: If fwd-status is not present but the fwd parameter is, it defaults to the status code sent in the response.
clauses.raw_text: If fwd-status is not present but the fwd parameter is, it defaults to the status code sent in the response.

clauses.normalized_text: This parameter is useful to distinguish cases when the next-hop server sends a 304 (Not Modified) response to a conditional request or a 206 (Partial Content) response because of a range request.
clauses.raw_text: This parameter is useful to distinguish cases when the next-hop server sends a 304 (Not Modified) response to a conditional request or a 206 (Partial Content) response because of a range request.

clauses.normalized_text: The value of "ttl" is an Integer that indicates the response's remaining freshness lifetime (see [HTTP-CACHING], Section 4.2.1) as calculated by the cache, as an integer number of seconds, measured as closely as possible to when the response header section is sent by the cache.
clauses.raw_text: The value of "ttl" is an Integer that indicates the response's remaining freshness lifetime (see [HTTP-CACHING], Section 4.2.1) as calculated by the cache, as an integer number of seconds, measured as closely as possible to when the response header section is sent by the cache.

clauses.normalized_text: This includes freshness assigned by the cache through, for example, heuristics (see [HTTP-CACHING], Section 4.2.2), local configuration, or other factors.
clauses.raw_text: This includes freshness assigned by the cache through, for example, heuristics (see [HTTP-CACHING], Section 4.2.2), local configuration, or other factors.

clauses.normalized_text: It may be negative, to indicate staleness.
clauses.raw_text: It may be negative, to indicate staleness.

clauses.normalized_text: The value of "stored" is a Boolean that indicates whether the cache stored the response (see [HTTP-CACHING], Section 3); a true value indicates that it did.
clauses.raw_text: The value of "stored" is a Boolean that indicates whether the cache stored the response (see [HTTP-CACHING], Section 3); a true value indicates that it did.

clauses.normalized_text: The stored parameter is only meaningful when fwd is present.
clauses.raw_text: The stored parameter is only meaningful when fwd is present.

clauses.normalized_text: The value of "collapsed" is a Boolean that indicates whether this request was collapsed together with one or more other forward requests (see [HTTP-CACHING], Section 4).
clauses.raw_text: The value of "collapsed" is a Boolean that indicates whether this request was collapsed together with one or more other forward requests (see [HTTP-CACHING], Section 4).

clauses.normalized_text: If true, the response was successfully reused; if not, a new request had to be made.
clauses.raw_text: If true, the response was successfully reused; if not, a new request had to be made.

clauses.normalized_text: If not present, the request was not collapsed with others.
clauses.raw_text: If not present, the request was not collapsed with others.

clauses.normalized_text: The collapsed parameter is only meaningful when fwd is present.
clauses.raw_text: The collapsed parameter is only meaningful when fwd is present.

clauses.normalized_text: The value of "key" is a String that conveys a representation of the cache key (see [HTTP-CACHING], Section 2) used for the response.
clauses.raw_text: The value of "key" is a String that conveys a representation of the cache key (see [HTTP-CACHING], Section 2) used for the response.

clauses.normalized_text: Note that this may be implementation specific.
clauses.raw_text: Note that this may be implementation specific.

clauses.normalized_text: The value of "detail" is either a String or a Token that allows implementations to convey additional information not captured in other parameters, such as implementation-specific states or other caching-related metrics.
clauses.raw_text: The value of "detail" is either a String or a Token that allows implementations to convey additional information not captured in other parameters, such as implementation-specific states or other caching-related metrics.

clauses.normalized_text: For example:
clauses.raw_text: For example:

clauses.normalized_text: Cache-Status: ExampleCache; hit; detail=MEMORY
clauses.raw_text: Cache-Status: ExampleCache; hit; detail=MEMORY

clauses.normalized_text: The semantics of a detail parameter are always specific to the cache that sent it; even if a details parameter from another cache shares the same value, it might not mean the same thing.
clauses.raw_text: The semantics of a detail parameter are always specific to the cache that sent it; even if a details parameter from another cache shares the same value, it might not mean the same thing.

clauses.normalized_text: This parameter is intentionally limited.
clauses.raw_text: This parameter is intentionally limited.

clauses.normalized_text: If an implementation's developer or operator needs to convey additional information in an interoperable fashion, they are encouraged to register extension parameters (see Section 4) or define another header field.
clauses.raw_text: If an implementation's developer or operator needs to convey additional information in an interoperable fashion, they are encouraged to register extension parameters (see Section 4) or define another header field.

clauses.normalized_text: The following is an example of going through two separate layers of caching, where the cache closest to the origin responded to an earlier request with a stored response, and a second cache stored that response and later reused it to satisfy the current request:

clauses.normalized_text: Attackers can use the information in Cache-Status to probe the behavior of the cache (and other components) and infer the activity of those using the cache.
clauses.raw_text: Attackers can use the information in Cache-Status to probe the behavior of the cache (and other components) and infer the activity of those using the cache.

clauses.normalized_text: The Cache-Status header field may not create these risks on its own, but it can assist attackers in exploiting them.
clauses.raw_text: The Cache-Status header field may not create these risks on its own, but it can assist attackers in exploiting them.

clauses.normalized_text: For example, knowing if a cache has stored a response can help an attacker execute a timing attack on sensitive data.
clauses.raw_text: For example, knowing if a cache has stored a response can help an attacker execute a timing attack on sensitive data.

clauses.normalized_text: Additionally, exposing the cache key can help an attacker understand modifications to the cache key, which may assist cache poisoning attacks.
clauses.raw_text: Additionally, exposing the cache key can help an attacker understand modifications to the cache key, which may assist cache poisoning attacks.

clauses.normalized_text: See [ENTANGLE] for details.
clauses.raw_text: See [ENTANGLE] for details.

clauses.normalized_text: The underlying risks can be mitigated with a variety of techniques (e.g., using encryption and authentication and avoiding the inclusion of attacker-controlled data in the cache key), depending on their exact nature.
clauses.raw_text: The underlying risks can be mitigated with a variety of techniques (e.g., using encryption and authentication and avoiding the inclusion of attacker-controlled data in the cache key), depending on their exact nature.

clauses.normalized_text: Note that merely obfuscating the key does not mitigate this risk.
clauses.raw_text: Note that merely obfuscating the key does not mitigate this risk.

clauses.normalized_text: To avoid assisting such attacks, the Cache-Status header field can be omitted, only sent when the client is authorized to receive it, or sent with sensitive information (e.g., the key parameter) only when the client is authorized.
clauses.raw_text: To avoid assisting such attacks, the Cache-Status header field can be omitted, only sent when the client is authorized to receive it, or sent with sensitive information (e.g., the key parameter) only when the client is authorized.
